annotation.method: Codex extracted and read all nine pages in physical order, covering Sections 1-5, every proposition, theorem, lemma, corollary and proof, all examples and comparisons, and all 16 references; separated the cited Chebyshev approximation theorem, spectral theory, and operator-algebra facts from the paper's own deductions; audited Mathlib and the exact frozen 44-object NumStability surface; and compiled exact private N/L proofs before retaining P56-T3.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P56 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.

rejected_candidates.reason: The reciprocal best-approximation formula is explicitly presented as a corollary of Chebyshev's result, so rebuilding it would turn cited approximation theory into a P56 proof obligation.

Their exact infinite-dimensional statements combine Proposition 2.1 with cited spectral theory. The frozen library has generic finite-matrix spectral wrappers but no band-support or Chebyshev-decay theorem, so it supplies neither a qualifying one-result nor two-result shortcut; supplying the cited approximation and spectral conclusions as assumptions leaves a much shorter deduction.

These results additionally use cited Calkin-algebra, compact-operator, open-mapping, or generalized-inverse background. No exact result obtains a substantial NumStability shortcut, and the self-contained new approximation work is isolated faithfully in Lemma 4.2.
Proposition 5.1's proof is omitted as a repetition of Proposition 2.2, and the examples are applications or qualitative illustrations rather than a better source-faithful tier target.

T1.decision: Skipped. No internally proved P56 result needs one substantial non-Mathlib declaration from the frozen library. Generic matrix spectral wrappers do not provide the missing Chebyshev or band-decay argument and are not a material one-result shortcut.

T2.decision: Skipped. No exact source-proved P56 result receives two distinct substantial compiled NumStability shortcuts; the central approximation and band-support arguments are absent from the library.

T3.decision: Selected the exact constructive heart of Lemma 4.2: extending an interval reciprocal approximant to finitely many exceptional positive points with controlled degree and a fixed multiplicative error constant. Exact N/L proofs establish substantial polynomial, interpolation, degree, and product-bound work with no NumStability shortcut.

selection_policy: Use only statements and proof content present in P56.
Treat Proposition 2.1 and the named spectral/operator facts as cited background rather than P56 proof obligations.
Represent Lemma 4.2 by the correction-polynomial construction and explicit constant proved in its text.
Do not replace infinite-dimensional cited theory with a stronger invented finite-matrix claim.
Assign a tier only after exact private N and L proofs compile.
